newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dates rescheduled for ADP air cargo task force.
newsitem.headline: Dates rescheduled for ADP air cargo task force.

text.p: The Paris airports authority, Aeroports de Paris (ADP), said its proposed air cargo task force to Latin America at the beginning of September 1997 had been put back to December due to "a number of minor factors."

"The new dates for the trip are December 8 to 10 with visits to Sao Paulo (Brazil), Buenos Aires (Argentina) and Santiago (Chile)," a spokesman for the ADP's freight marketing department told Reuters.
All three of these cities are served with scheduled air cargo services by Air France.

"This will be the task force's first trip to Latin America, a region which generates relatively minor air cargo volumes in relation to North America and the Far East but whose rate of growth is among the strongest in the industry," the spokesman said.

The main aim of the trip was to promote the Paris airports as a gateway for air cargo in addressing air freight forwarding agents and other industry professionals as well as shippers, the spokesman added.
The task force will include representatives from ADP, Air France Cargo, French agents association SNAGFA as well as customs.
The ADP's air cargo task force had also re-arranged the dates of its trade mission to the U.S.
"We had scheduled the trip for early November just after the Air Cargo Americas trade fair in Miami but on reflection decided it would be better to conduct it before this event takes place."
The new dates for the U.S. trip were October 22 to 28 encompassing visits to Houston, Atlanta and Miami.

"Atlanta and Houston are respectively the hubs of Delta and Continental and the two airlines' alliances with Air France, which includes freight traffic, will provide the backdrop to the task force' visit."
Air France operates scheduled cargo services to Miami and Houston and ad hoc full-freighters to Atlanta.
